content: Nin Jiom Pei Pa Koa, also known as King-to Nin Jiom Pei Pa Koa or simply Pei Pa Koa, is a traditional Chinese herbal remedy designed to alleviate symptoms such as sore throat, cough, hoarseness, and loss of voice. It functions as both a throat demulcent and an expectorant. The product is currently manufactured and distributed globally by Nin Jiom Medicine Manufactory Limited, a company based in Hong Kong. The name King-to refers to Beijing, while Nin Jiom translates to in memory of my mother, and Pei Pa Koa means Loquat syrup. The original formula for Pei Pa Koa was developed by Doctor Ip Tin-See, a physician during the Qing Dynasty. The remedy was created at the request of Yang Xiao-Lian, a provincial commander, to treat his mother’s persistent cough. The results were so effective that the Yang family decided to establish a factory to produce the remedy on a larger scale. Eventually, the business was sold to Tse Sui-Bong, a practitioner of medicine. In 1962, Nin Jiom Medicine Manufacturing was officially incorporated to further expand the production and distribution of Pei Pa Koa. Today, the product generates annual sales of approximately 45 million USD. A pharmacological study conducted by the China Academy of Traditional Chinese Medicine, published in 1994, demonstrated that Pei Pa Koa has significant efficacy in relieving coughs, promoting the removal of sputum, and alleviating asthma symptoms. These effects were observed in both in vivo and in vitro studies. The composition of Pei Pa Koa includes a combination of various herbal ingredients. These include fritillary bulb (Chuan Bei Mu), loquat leaf (Pi Pa Ye), ladybell root (Nan Sha Shen), poria cocos (Fu Ling), pomelo peel (Mao Ju Hong), Chinese bellflower root (Jie Geng), pinellia rhizome (Ban Xia), schisandra chinensis seed (Wu Wei Zi), trichosanthes seed (Gua Lou Zi), coltsfoot flower (Guan Dong Hua), thinleaf milkwort root (Yuan Zhi), bitter apricot kernel (Ku Xing Ren), fresh ginger (Shen Jiang), and licorice root (Gan Cao). These ingredients are combined in a syrup and honey base to create the final product.
